newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand mulls lifting animal feed import quota.
newsitem.headline: Thailand mulls lifting animal feed import quota.

text.p: The Thai government is considering lifting the import quota on animal feed raw materials such as soymeal, soybean and corn, industry sources said on Tuesday.

Commerce Minister Chucheep Harnsawat, in his capacity as chairman of the Food Policy Committee, met with representatives of oil crushing and animal feed industries on Monday to seek their opinion on the issue, said a source from the oil crushing industry who attended the meeting.
"At this point, both sides seemed to reach a consensus that the quota should be lifted. However, the government is looking for measures to protect local farmers," the source said.
The government plans to lift import quotas on animal feed raw materials by the year 1997 and let people in the industry import freely.
It is also considering cutting the import tariff to zero percent from 5.0 percent for soybean, and to 10.0 percent from 15.0 percent for soymeal.

The moves are intended to stabilise and cut production costs for the poultry and meat industry. The high and fluctuating prices of animal feed raw materials have been blamed for high prices of meat in the local market.
Industry sources said it was not clear when the decision would be finalised.

The Thai government earlier imposed the import quota on certain agricultural products to protect local farmers. Estimated industry demand and local output projection were considered before the government determined the amount allowed under the annual import quota.
